fold.title: Fold tracks
fold.into_tip: How many tracks the notes end up on. It starts at the number of colours the notes use. Drag the word or use Up / Down to step it.
fold.in_a_row_tip: Tracks next to each other go together: the first group of tracks becomes track 1, the next group track 2, and so on. Thin stripes of many colours become wide bands of one colour.
fold.looping_tip: The tracks are dealt out in turn: with 16 tracks, tracks 1, 17, 33 … become track 1, tracks 2, 18, 34 … track 2, and so on. The colours mostly stay as they look now, on fewer tracks.
fold.keep_example: each colour folds on its own
fold.cut_tip: Notes on the same key that now overlap in one track are fixed like Single channel does: the earlier note is cut where the later one starts, and notes starting together become one. Untick to keep both.
fold.even_tip: In a row: every group gets about the same number of tracks. Unticked, the groups are full and the last one is left short.
fold.keep_tip: Each new track takes notes of one colour only, so the picture stays the same and every track stays on one channel. Fold into can't go below the number of colours then.
fold.short: (full groups can't make {n}: tick Even groups)
fold.nothing: These notes have no tracks to fold.
fold.name: {name} (folded)
fill_gaps.title: Fill gaps
fill_gaps.same_start: Notes starting on the same tick of a key:
fill_gaps.hint_right: Each note's end moves to the next note's start on its key. The last note of each key row stays as it is.
fill_gaps.hint_left: Each note's start moves back to the end of the note before it on its key (the timing changes). The first note of each key row stays as it is.
fill_gaps.hint_middle: Both notes stretch toward each other and meet halfway in the gap. The first and last note of each key row stay as they are.
fill_gaps.left_out: Hz bass, images and masks are left out.
fill_gaps.nothing: Select the shapes whose gaps you want to fill (not Hz bass, images or masks).
fill_gaps.no_gaps: Nothing to fill: there are no gaps between these notes.
fill_gaps.done: Filled the gaps: {n} shapes are plain notes now
fill_gaps.done_one: Filled the gaps: the shape is plain notes now
lines.gap: Join notes with gaps up to
lines.gap_tip: Notes on the same key or a neighbouring key are one line when they touch. Raise this to also join notes that many ticks apart (0 = only touching notes).
lines.bad_gap: Type a whole number of ticks, 0 or more.
lines.hint_sideways: Each line is mirrored in time inside its own place: it starts and ends where it did, the notes inside run the other way.
lines.hint_upside: Each line is mirrored inside its own keys: its highest and lowest keys swap, every note keeps its time.
lines.drawn_ask: {n} drawn shapes need to turn into plain notes first to go on. Turn them into plain notes?
lines.drawn_ask_one: The drawn shape needs to turn into plain notes first to go on. Turn it into plain notes?
lines.nothing: Select shapes with notes (not Hz bass, images or masks).
lines.no_change: Nothing to flip: every line already looks the same flipped.
lines.align_tip: For lines of different lengths (a shape cut at an edge): after the flip they bunch up in one place. Ticked, every whole line then moves up or down until it touches the highest or lowest note. Only keys change: times, lengths and notes stay. The shape covers fewer keys, but the lines sit neatly side by side.
lines.align_up_tip: Each line moves up until its top touches the highest note of the selected shapes.
lines.align_down_tip: Each line moves down until its bottom touches the lowest note of the selected shapes.
lines.align_remove_tip: After lining up, notes on the same key that overlap another note go (the first one stays). Unticked, every note stays.
lines.hint_split: Each line becomes its own track: the first stays where it is, the next ones go on new tracks right under it (same channel, ports B to P, then round the ports again).
lines.split_none: Nothing to split: every track of the selected shapes holds one line.
lines.split_done: Split off {n} pieces onto new tracks
lines.split_done_one: Split off 1 piece onto a new track
lines.split_shared: (more than {most} pieces on one track: the ports ran out, so the later pieces share ports and channels with the first ones)
lines.split_too_many: This would make {n} tracks, more than a MIDI file can hold ({most}). Nothing was changed.
merge_window.hint_right: The leftmost shape slides right: each key row until it meets the other shapes' notes.
merge_window.hint_left: The rightmost shape slides left: each key row until it meets the other shapes' notes.
merge_window.hint_up: The shape with the lowest note is cut where the other shapes' notes start and end. Each piece slides up until it meets them (nothing in its way: up to the top key).
merge_window.hint_down: The shape with the highest note is cut where the other shapes' notes start and end. Each piece slides down until it meets them (nothing in its way: down to the lowest key).
join_split.merge_no_notes: A selected shape has no notes: nothing to merge.
join_split.merge_two_only: Without "Keep shapes separate", only two shapes can be merged at once.
join_split.merge_no_room_up: No room to slide it out under the other shape (key 0 or another shape is in the way): nothing merged.
join_split.merge_no_room_down: No room to slide it out over the other shape (the top key or another shape is in the way): nothing merged.
join_split.merge_no_room_side: No room to slide it out past the other shape (another shape is in the way): nothing merged.
join_split.merged_one_up_down_done: Merged: each piece slid until it met the other shape's notes.
join_split.merged_one_up_wall: Merged. Some pieces had nothing in their way: they went up to the top key and are a shape of their own now ("Merge leftovers").
join_split.merged_one_down_wall: Merged. Some pieces had nothing in their way: they went down to the lowest key and are a shape of their own now ("Merge leftovers").
join_split.merge_mask_mixed: A mask and a shape that isn't one can't be merged (the mask's notes are only a preview): nothing merged.
merge_window.need_two: Select two or more shapes to merge.

join_split.merged_apart_left: Merged. {n} key rows had nothing to meet: they slid as little as the row that slid least and are a shape of their own now ("Merge leftovers"). The shape that slid is fixed notes now (Split gives it back).
join_split.merged_apart_left_one: Merged. 1 key row had nothing to meet: it slid as little as the row that slid least and is a shape of its own now ("Merge leftovers"). The shape that slid is fixed notes now (Split gives it back).

join_split.split_in_two_baked: Split in two (its formula became a plain curve first, so each half keeps its part)

join_split.made_complete_n: {n} complete shapes now: their notes follow their own lines

join_split.plain_done_one: Turned the shape into plain notes, each note on the channel it had

join_split.slice_merged: A merged shape can't be sliced. Turn it into plain notes first (right-click → Turn into plain notes), then slice it

join_split.slice_merged_too_one: . 1 merged shape stays whole: turn it into plain notes first to slice it

join_split.slice_flat_missed: A flat slice line cuts pasted notes into the notes above it and the rest: draw it through the notes, with notes above and below it
join_split.slice_partly_too: . {n} shapes weren't crossed all the way, so they stay whole
join_split.slice_partly_too_one: . 1 shape wasn't crossed all the way, so it stays whole

join_split.knife_cut_one: Cut 1 shape with "{name}": the part under it is selected

join_split.knife_whole_one: Nothing to cut: 1 shape is wholly under "{name}", so it's selected

join_split.knife_click: Click a shape to cut with it: everything under its notes becomes its own piece
join_split.knife_cant: Only custom shapes, pasted notes and text can cut (not lines, pictures, masks, merged shapes or Hz bass)
join_split.knife_no_notes: "{name}" has no notes, so it can't cut anything

mask.tick_tip: While ticked, whatever you draw becomes a mask: a preview that shows the shapes under it only inside it (the rest faint). Nothing is cut: the shapes under it stay whole and still sound. Works with Live shape too (paint with the mask).
mask.preview_tip: Ticked: masks preview their cut, the parts of the shapes under them outside the mask drawn faint. Unticked: the shapes under masks are drawn whole, only the masks' dashed lines show. Nothing changes in the sound or the file either way, and Apply mask works the same.
mask.fade_tip: How much of the hidden parts still shows, in their own colours: 0 % = not drawn at all, 100 % = as solid as the other notes. Only changes what you see.
mask.label: Mask: {label}
mask.panel_tip: A mask shows the shapes under it only inside it; the rest is drawn faint. The shapes under it don't change and still sound. Untick to make it a normal shape again.
mask.own_tip: Ticked: the mask's own notes sound like any shape's, as a border. Unticked: it's a pure cutter, only its dashed line shows.
mask.thickness_tip: How thick the band round the mask's notes is, in keys. It's even all the way round, in the proportions the piano roll had when the shape became a mask. With Inside it widens the inside past the outline (0 = just the inside).
mask.thickness_solid: A Fill or Spam mask shows its whole inside, so it has no thickness.
mask.show_tip: Inside: the shapes under it show inside its outline, between its own notes. Along the line: only in a band round its line.
mask.invert_tip: Ticked: the shapes under the mask show everywhere except inside it, like a cookie cutter making a hole.
mask.apply_tip: Makes a new shape of the notes the mask shows, exactly as you see them. The shapes under it don't change, and the mask stays, so you can move it and apply it again. While Own notes sound is ticked, its border notes are copied too. A mask in a group applies the whole group. Invert masks over the same shape apply together: one copy with all their holes.
mask.apply_nothing: Nothing applied: no notes show through the mask
mask.apply_done: Made {shapes} holding {notes}, as the mask shows them; the shapes under it didn't change
mask.mode_tip: How this mask joins the masks above it in its group (Shapes list order, top first). Add: the pattern also shows inside this one. Subtract: this one cuts it away. Intersect: only where this one and the ones above overlap.
mask.mode_first: The first mask in a group always adds.
mask.combine_done: Combined: {n} masks now work as one group. Set each one's Mode in the side panel
mask.separate_done: Separated: each of these masks works on its own again

paste.title: Paste colours
paste.intro: Paste any text with colours in it (a whole settings file is fine):
paste.legend: Blue = the colours that will be used.   Grey = found, not used.   Struck out = switched-off line, skipped ({n}).
paste.lock: Lock them: the image uses exactly these colours (right-click a colour later to free it)
paste.start: Only a starting point: Spiderweb may change them to fit the image better
paste.ch10_left: Channel 10 isn't used (drums): the image gets the other 15.
app.slice_modes_tip: ▾ = Slice (draw a line to cut along) or Slice with shape (click a shape: everything under its notes is cut out as its own piece, the shape stays; also on the right-click of a shape lying over others).
app.lasso_tip: Draw a loop round notes, then press Enter to cut them along it: the part inside is selected. Esc throws the loop away. ▾ = Lasso (drag), Polygonal (click points) or Magnetic (clings to the notes).
panel_lasso.cut_tip: Cut along the loop (Enter). Before the loop is closed: closes it.
panel_lasso.width_tip: Magnetic: how far from the mouse it looks for a note's corner to cling to
panel_lasso.none: Draw a loop on the piano roll
pianoroll.lasso_magnet: Move the mouse round the notes: the line clings to them, never cutting one. Click = a point by hand; click the first point, double-click, right-click or press Enter to close. Backspace = last points off, [ ] = Width
pianoroll.lasso_draw: Drag round the notes; let go to close the loop. Hold Alt for straight lines
pianoroll.lasso_poly: Click points (on the snap grid; Ctrl = free); click the first point, double-click, right-click or press Enter to close. Backspace = last point off, Shift = 45°, Alt-drag = freehand
pianoroll.lasso_ready: Enter = cut along the loop, Esc = throw it away. Drag its points; Alt-drag a point = curve handles, Alt-drag a handle = a corner; middle-click the loop = add a point, right-click a point = handles off, then remove it
app.tools_list_tip: Every drawing tool. Pick one and this button shows it, so one click picks it again. The pin on a tool's right gives it its own button here.
app.pin_tip: Pin: give this tool its own button in the toolbar. Click again to take the button away.
app.keeps_overlaps_every_note_exactly_as:
Keeps overlaps.
Every note exactly as the shapes make it, all on one channel.
Notes on the same key can overlap or start on the same tick.
app.removes_overlaps_all_on_one_channel:
Removes overlaps, all on one channel.
Where two notes on the same key overlap, the earlier one is cut
where the later one starts, and the later one is stretched
to where the earlier one would have ended.
Notes starting on the same tick become one note: the loudest wins,
and it's as long as the longest of them.
app.a_channel_per_overlap_shapes_whose:
A channel per overlap.
Shapes whose notes overlap go on different channels, each on its own
track (channel 10 is skipped). Shapes that don't clash share a channel.
The box below picks what counts as an overlap.
app.split_same_key_at_the_same: Split: same key at the same time
app.split_any_notes_at_the_same: Split: any notes at the same time
app.ch10_order_tip:
Shapes take channels 1, 2, 3 … 16 in order, so a shape's 10th colour goes on channel 10.
Off: channel 10 comes last (1-9, 11-16, then 10), so ticking Use channel 10 changes no colour.
When 10 or more channels are in use, the 10th and later change colour when this is switched,
because each channel keeps its own colour. Saved with the project.
app.channels_fold_tip:
Click to fold or unfold the channel settings.
Folded, the grey words say what's turned on.
app.single_split_tip:
Off: where two notes overlap on one key, the earlier note is cut where the later one starts,
and the later one is stretched to where the earlier one would have ended.
On: the later note keeps its own length, and what's left of the earlier note after it
comes back as a note of its own (more notes, gaps look even). Saved with the project.
app.multi_cut_tip:
Shapes still get their own channels, and on top of that no two notes sound on one key at once,
so no player cuts them at random. The track order (as in the track list) decides which note wins.
Saved with the project.
app.multi_win_tip:
Earlier tracks win: a note on an earlier track cuts the overlapping notes of later tracks.
Later tracks win: the other way round. Earlier = higher up in the track list.
app.multi_stretch_tip:
Off: the losing note is split around the winning one: cut where it starts,
and what's left after it ends comes back as a note of its own (more notes, gaps look even).
On: the losing note is only cut, and the winning note is stretched over what's left, like Single channel.
Pieces as short as 1 tick are kept either way.
app.pad_rounds_tip:
On: each time the colours repeat (or a shape moves to the next row of channels, Settings → Note colours),
all 15 channels (16 with channel 10) get a track in the MIDI file and Export to Domino, empty tracks for the colours that row doesn't use.
Off: only tracks with notes are written. Every note keeps its channel and colour either way.
Saved with the project.
app.new_rounds_tip:
When a shape's colours start again from the first colour, the repeated colours go on new channels
with the same colours (15 channels further on, 16 with channel 10). A channel never holds a colour twice,
so each repeat can be edited on its own in other programs. Counts for Colours, Nested and Tiles fills,
Add between steps, Copy along a path's colours, and area or outline colours used on separate parts
of one shape (a merged shape too). Other shapes keep the first channels.
Saved with the project.
app.pasted_15: {n} pasted shapes had 16 colours: brought down to 15 (this project doesn't use channel 10).
app.pasted_15_one: 1 pasted shape had 16 colours: brought down to 15 (this project doesn't use channel 10).
app.pasted_picture_15: {n} pasted images had 16 colours: brought down to 15 (this project's images don't use channel 10).
app.pasted_picture_15_one: 1 pasted image had 16 colours: brought down to 15 (this project's images don't use channel 10).
app.use_ch10_tip:
Shapes may use channel 10 too, so there are 16 colours instead of 15.
Many synths play channel 10 as drums (with a piano-only soundfont, MIDI players stay silent there).
Built-in BASSMIDI plays it as a piano. Saved with the project.
app.same_key_shapes_only_get_split:
Same key: shapes only get split when they play the same key at the same time.
Any notes: shapes get split whenever their notes play at the same time,
even on different keys (e.g. two parallel lines, or lines starting on the
same tick). Shapes that follow one after another still share a channel.
snap.tip:
The grid points and notes snap to while you draw and drag (Shift = don't snap).
Note lengths: 1/4 = a quarter note (one beat), 3/8 = a dotted quarter, 1/6 = quarter-note triplets.
Custom… = any length you set up.
snap.kind_tip:
Empty = one plain note (16 = a 16th note), the left number isn't used.
/ = that many notes (3 / 16 = three 16th notes).
. = a dotted note (one and a half notes), .. = double dotted (one and three quarters).
snap.divided_by_tip: Splits the length into this many equal steps (3 = triplets).
app.tempo_pane_tip: Under the piano roll: the tempo line (BPM changes, stops and catch-ups), time signatures and key signatures for the MIDI export.
tempo.play_bpm_tip: The exact tempo (BPM) at the play line, as the MIDI file holds it.
tempo.play_heard_tip: Inside a Keep timing part: the tempo really heard at the play line (the notes keep their time at it).
conductor.top_range: The top number must be a whole number from {lo} to {hi}.
tempo.every_tip: Ticks between the tempo changes a curved part writes (and a curved catch-up). 1 = a change on every tick; many MIDI programs draw lines every 24.
tempo.scale_tip: Linear: the same BPM added every beat (60 to 240 passes 150 halfway). Exponential: the BPM grows by the same amount of doubling every beat, straight on this pane's scale (60 to 240 passes 120 halfway), good for huge spikes.
tempo.catch_end_auto: End the catch-up at the next point
tempo.keep_dense: Keep timing: notes too close (tempo stays faster)
tempo.hint_on_dense: Notes too close for this part's slower tempo: it stays faster here, the timing is still right. A higher PPQ helps.
tempo.keep_tip: Keep the audio: the notes sound at the heard tempo (the purple line) while the file shows this part's tempo; the export moves them in ticks. Keep the visual: the file keeps showing its tempo while the sound follows the heard line. Switching swaps the two lines.
tempo.keeps_tip: Keep timing for every part between the picked points (they become one Keep timing part)
tempo.hint_on_start: Drag: the time this catch-up counts (the yellow area's start) · Right-click: menu
tempo.hint_on_end: Drag: where this catch-up's BPM stops (the teal area's end) · Right-click: menu
tempo.keep_in_catch_refused: Keep timing doesn't work inside a catch-up's yellow area: move the part or the catch-up first
tempo.keep_in_catch: Keep timing: off inside the catch-up
tempo.hint_on_keep_off: Keep timing is off here: this part is inside a catch-up's yellow area, which counts its time
tempo.paste_no_catch: Pasted the points only: catch-ups go in the visual tempo (Draw: Visual tempo)

{bpm} BPM here

app.formula_tip: Drag a line like Linear: a pattern (Wave, Zigzag, Bounce or one you saved) swings the velocity up and down around it. Its settings show next to the tool buttons; changing them changes the line you just drew.
app.ctrl_flat_shift_snap_enter_done: Ctrl = flat · Shift = snap · Enter = done · select a shape to edit only its notes
app.a_ppq_of_or_more_many:
A PPQ of {PPQ_WARN} or more: many MIDI programs can't open the file.
Spiderweb still writes it.
app.edo31_tip:
Shows the piano roll in 31-EDO: 31 keys an octave instead of 12 (key 0 = C0).
White keys = the 7 plain notes, black keys = sharps and flats, grey keys = half sharps (^) and half flats (v).
Only the look changes: the saved MIDI keeps the same key numbers.
app.edo31_audio_tip:
Playback and right-drag listening sound in 31-EDO too, every key up to 255.
Only with Built-in BASSMIDI or Kestrel (GPU) as the MIDI out.
app.edo31_audio_needs_builtin:
Audio is ticked, but the MIDI out isn't Built-in BASSMIDI, Kestrel (GPU) or Rendered ahead, so playback plays the usual way (keys above 127 are skipped).
Pick one of them in Settings (Help menu) → Sound to hear 31-EDO.
app.edo31_audio_builtin_only: 31-EDO Audio only works with Built-in BASSMIDI, Kestrel (GPU) or Rendered ahead: playing as usual.
app.128_the_standard_keys_0_127:
128: the standard keys 0–127, which every MIDI program reads.
256: keys 0–255, for players that support them (handy for tunings like 31edo).
Many MIDI programs can't read keys above 127, and playback here skips them (unless 31-EDO Audio is on).
app.voices_tip:
How many sounds Built-in BASSMIDI can ring at once (1000 to start). More = fuller in busy parts, but more work for the processor: if playback breaks up ("Overloaded" in red next to the Settings button), lower it.
Past the limit, the oldest sounds are cut.
app.offrange_tip: Notes outside the valid key range or before bar 1. They are kept only in the project file: not exported, played or copied to other programs.
app.offrange_tip_wrap:
Notes outside the valid key range or before bar 1, kept in the project file.
Wrap them around is on: the ones past the keys are exported, played and copied wrapped around onto the keys. The ones before bar 1 are left out.

bs.title: Built-in BASSMIDI settings
bs.guard: Lower it by itself when overloaded
bs.guard_tip: Ticked: while the processor can't make the sound fast enough (it stops or crackles), the voice limit is lowered until it keeps up, then quickly raised back to yours once it's calm. Each Play starts from your limit (moving the play line while it plays keeps the lowered one).
bs.synths_tip: A loaded MIDI plays on this many synths side by side, each on its own processor core, so busy parts of dense MIDIs can sound fuller (half your cores to start). More = fewer notes left out in the busiest parts, but less room for the rest of your PC: lower it if your PC slows down while playing. Heard from the next Play.
bs.slow_down_tip: Ticked: when the processor can't make the sound fast enough, the song plays slower instead (down to 10 %), the pitch the same, and goes back to its own speed once it can. With "Lower it by itself when overloaded" ticked too, the voice limit is lowered only once it's at the slowest, or once playing slower stops helping (very many notes ringing at once). Busy loaded MIDIs can slow down a lot. Heard at once.
bs.limiter_tip: Ticked: sound louder than full volume is turned down instead of clipped (clipping = a harsh, broken sound in busy parts), so busy parts sound cleaner but flatter. Off: too loud is clipped. Heard at once.
bs.limiter_slow: The compiled loops aren't working here, so playback may break up for a moment while you edit with it on.
ks.title: Kestrel (GPU, Experimental) settings
ks.voices_tip: The most notes Kestrel lets sound at once (300,000 to start). More = busy parts keep more of their ringing notes and sound fuller, but each block takes the graphics card longer and very heavy MIDIs may fall behind. You can type 300k, 1m, 1.5mil and so on. Used from the next Play (Kestrel starts again, a few seconds).
ks.voices_default_tip: Max voices back to {n} (only this box).
ks.lower: Lower it by itself when it can't keep up
ks.lower_tip: Ticked: when the graphics card can't make the sound in time, the quietest notes are left out (each channel keeps its share) so playback never stops. Off: every note plays, and playback stutters where it can't keep up. Heard at once.
ks.slow_down_tip: Ticked: when the graphics card can't make the sound in time, the song plays slower instead (down to 10 %), the pitch the same, and goes back to its own speed once it can. With "Lower it by itself" ticked too, notes are left out only once it's at the slowest, or once playing slower stops helping (very many notes ringing at once). Heard at once.
ks.block_tip: Kestrel makes the sound this many samples at a time. Bigger = easier for the graphics card in busy parts, but the sound comes a little later after Play. Used from the next Play.
ks.limiter_tip: What happens to sound louder than the ceiling. Balanced = first evens out long loud parts a little, then turns down only the peaks, so busy parts keep more of their punch (Kestrel's own renders use it). Brickwall = only turns down what goes over the ceiling, a little flatter in busy parts. Off = too loud is clipped (a harsh, broken sound). Used from the next Play.
ks.ceiling_tip: The loudest the limiter lets the sound get, in dB below full volume: 0 = full volume, -1 = a little under it (leaves room so nothing clips later), down to -24. Decimals work (-0.5). Used from the next Play.
ks.dc_tip: Ticked: takes out the slow drift away from the middle that thousands of notes can add up to, which otherwise eats the limiter's room and makes the bass sound off. Used from the next Play.
ks.card_tip: Which graphics card Kestrel plays on. Automatic picks the strongest one (a laptop's own graphics card rather than the one built into the processor). Vulkan and DirectX 12 are two ways of talking to the same card: if one stutters or fails, try the other. Changing it sends the soundfonts to the card again (a moment).
ks.card_gone: The graphics card picked for Kestrel ({card}) wasn't found, so it played on the strongest one (Settings → Sound: back to Automatic).
ks.card_failed: The graphics card picked for Kestrel ({card}) couldn't start it, so it plays on the strongest one until Spiderweb is started again (Settings → Sound: try the card's other entry, or Automatic).
ks.interp_tip: How the soundfont's recordings are played higher or lower than they were recorded. Nearest = fastest, a bit grainy on high notes. Linear = Kestrel's usual. Cubic = smoothest, more work for the graphics card. Heard from the next Play (while playing: Kestrel starts again from the play line).
ks.min_vel_tip: Notes with a velocity under this aren't played at all (0 = every note). Dense MIDIs often hide many very quiet notes: leaving them out is much less work. Heard from the next Play (while playing: Kestrel starts again from the play line).
ra.title: Rendered ahead settings
ra.engine_tip: What makes the sound ahead of the play line. Merlin: the fastest, every note played, but some controllers aren't exact yet. Kestrel: slower, exact. BASSMIDI: on the processor, works on any PC. Used from the next Play.
ra.while_stopped_tip: Ticked: while playing is stopped, the sound is made from the play line (once it rests half a second) up to Render ahead seconds, so a heavy song can be waited out before Play: the faint grey clears as it's made, and Play starts at once with what's made. Moving the play line makes from the new place; what was made elsewhere is kept for a while.
ra.exact: Use Kestrel where Merlin isn't exact
ra.exact_tip: Merlin doesn't play controllers exactly yet (volume, expression, pan, sustain pedal and CC lines other than pitch bends), in your shapes and in a loaded MIDI. Unticked: Merlin makes them anyway, fast but a little off. Ticked: songs with them are made with Kestrel, exact but much slower (the status line says so). Used from the next Play.
ra.starting_card: Rendered ahead: putting the soundfont on the graphics card…
ra.starting: Rendered ahead: making the first seconds… {n} / {m}
ra.fonts_note: More than one soundfont is in the list: Merlin can't use several yet, so Kestrel makes the sound (slower).
ra.seconds_tip: How far ahead of the play line the sound is made (5 to 300 seconds). Playing starts once the first 5 seconds are made; making goes on in the background, keeping this far ahead. More = fewer waits in busy parts, but more memory.
ra.slow_down_tip: Ticked: when the play line catches up with the part not made yet (faint grey in the piano roll), playing waits there until the sound is ready, then goes on. Unticked: the play line keeps the song's speed, a part not made in time stays silent, and making jumps ahead to just past the play line.
ra.card_tip: Which graphics card makes the sound ahead. The same setting as Kestrel's live play: changing one changes both. Automatic picks the strongest one. Vulkan and DirectX 12 are two ways of talking to the same card: if one fails, try the other.
ra.voices_tip: The most notes Kestrel lets sound at once while making the sound ahead (1,048,576 to start: more than live play's, since nothing has to sound at once). Fewer = each piece is made faster, but busy parts lose ringing notes. You can type 300k, 1m and so on. Used from the next Play.
ra.bass_voices_tip: How many sounds BASSMIDI can ring at once while making the sound ahead (1000 to start). More = fuller in busy parts, each piece takes the processor longer to make. Past the limit, the oldest sounds are cut. Used from the next Play.
ra.lower: Lower it by itself when falling behind
ra.lower_tip: Ticked: when the sound made ahead of the play line runs low (under a quarter of Render ahead, at least 3 seconds), the next pieces are made with fewer voices so they're ready sooner, and it climbs back slowly once there's plenty again. Pieces made with fewer voices are made again at the full limit later, while they're still ahead of the play line. With Slow down to keep up ticked too, this comes first; playing waits only if it still isn't enough.
ra.block_tip: The graphics card makes the sound this many samples at a time. Bigger = easier for a weaker graphics card. Here it doesn't delay the sound (it's made ahead anyway). Used from the next Play.
ra.interp_tip: How the soundfont's recordings are played higher or lower than they were recorded. Nearest = fastest, a bit grainy on high notes. Linear = Kestrel's usual. Cubic = smoothest, more work for the graphics card. Used from the next Play.
ra.min_vel_tip: Notes with a velocity under this aren't played at all (0 = every note). Leaving out very quiet notes is much less work. Used from the next Play.
ra.limiter_tip: What happens to sound louder than the ceiling, over the whole made sound (no jumps where pieces meet). Balanced = first evens out long loud parts a little, then turns down only the peaks. Brickwall = only turns down what goes over the ceiling. Off = too loud is clipped (a harsh, broken sound). Used from the next Play.
ra.kestrel_cc: Rendered ahead: made with Kestrel here (Merlin doesn't play CC lines exactly yet, only pitch bends).
ra.kestrel_fonts: Rendered ahead: made with Kestrel here (Merlin can't use more than one soundfont yet).
ks.voices_lowered: Max voices was more than this graphics card can take, so it was lowered to {n}, the most it can take (Settings → Sound).
ks.next_play: Changing a Kestrel setting (except Lower it by itself and Slow down) while playing starts Kestrel again with it from the play line (a few seconds).
ks.restarting: Kestrel's settings changed: starting it again with them from the play line…
ks.why_no_gpu: No graphics card Kestrel can use was found. Kestrel needs a fairly recent graphics card with an up-to-date driver: updating the graphics driver may help.
ks.why_memory: The graphics card ran out of memory. A lower Max voices (Settings → Sound) may help.
ks.why_lost: The graphics card or its driver was reset. Playing again may work; if it keeps happening, updating the graphics driver may help.
ks.why_font: A soundfont couldn't be read by Kestrel.
ks.why_connector: Kestrel's connector file in this copy of Spiderweb is damaged or from another version. Downloading Spiderweb again should fix it.
ks.why_slow: Kestrel didn't start in time (the graphics driver may be stuck).
ks.why_stuck: Kestrel stopped answering: it made no sound for a few seconds (the graphics driver may be stuck). Playing again may work; if it keeps happening, updating the graphics driver may help.
ks.slow_start: This is taking longer than usual.
ks.keep_ask:
Kestrel (GPU, Experimental) has read the busiest parts of {name} ahead. Keep this read-ahead ({size}) next to the MIDI's saved index, so they are ready in a moment next time?

Without it they are read again each time the MIDI is loaded (this time it took {s} s). Settings → Loaded MIDI lists saved indexes; deleting one deletes its read-ahead too.
ks.keep_failed: Kestrel's read-ahead couldn't be kept (the disk may be full, or the MIDI's saved index was deleted). It's read again next time.

app.where_copied_and_pasted_notes_start:
Where copied and pasted notes start:
First note at tick 0: the first note lands right on the cursor / play line.
From the bar line: the empty space from the bar line before the first note
comes along, so the notes keep their place in the bar.
app.domino_paste_tip:
Paste from Domino: the notes copied in Domino (Ctrl+C there) become one shape here.
It starts at the play line, like pasting in Domino (see the start setting above).
Every track's notes go into the one shape; controllers and other events are left out.
Ticks are taken as they are: use the same PPQ here.
Ctrl+V pastes them too, when they were copied last.
app.domino_export_tip:
Export to Domino: saves every note as a Domino song file (.dms), next to the MIDI file
in the Output file box, with the same name.
It can hold a PPQ up to 65535 (a MIDI file stops at 32767).
Each channel gets its own track, like Export MIDI.
app.ctrl_shift_c_copies_the_selected:
Copy to Domino (Ctrl+Shift+C): copies the selected shapes' notes (all notes when nothing is selected).
In Domino, paste with Ctrl+V at the cursor, or double-click in the piano roll.
Multi channel: each channel goes into its own track, from that one down.
Ticks are copied as they are: use the same PPQ there.
The other way: notes copied in Domino paste here with Ctrl+V or a Select double-click.
project.cc_lost: {n:,} pasted notes shapes had CCs that couldn't be read (damaged). Their notes are here, the CCs are left out.
project.cc_lost_one: 1 pasted notes shape had CCs that couldn't be read (damaged). Its notes are here, the CCs are left out.
project.cc_not_written: Its CCs are only sent with Multi channel (Project → Channels), or when it is pasted with a track highlighted in the track list.
project.cc_left_out_midi: {n:,} of the pasted notes' events are Domino's own (no MIDI message for them), so they're left out of the MIDI file. Export to Domino keeps them.
project.cc_left_out_midi_one: 1 of the pasted notes' events is Domino's own (no MIDI message for it), so it's left out of the MIDI file. Export to Domino keeps it.
project.cc_single_channel: The pasted notes' CCs aren't in the file: they're only written with Multi channel (Project → Channels), or for notes pasted with a track highlighted in the track list.
app.side_strip_tip: Show the side panel. Click to open it, or drag it out to the width you want.
app.new_ask:
Start a new MIDI?

Every shape and the Conductor (tempo, time and key signatures) are cleared. PPQ, Keys, the output file and channel settings stay.
This can't be undone.
app.glued: Glued touching notes: {notes} → {after}. The shape remembers it: right-click → Remove glue takes it off
app.velocity_drawn_in_the_velocity_pane: Velocity drawn in the velocity pane. Typing a start/end here goes back to a straight ramp.
app.starts_exactly_on_the_last_point: starts exactly on the last point
app.by_snap_end_tip:
For a line that isn't a whole number of steps long:
Last step cut short: every step is full, the last one ends exactly on the line's last point.
Full last step: the last step is full too, so it can go past the last point.
Whole steps only: only the whole steps that fit, the keys squeezed into them; it can end before the last point.
Steps stretched to fit: every step a little longer or shorter so they end exactly on the last point (off the grid).
app.by_snap_tip:
Every note is one step long, so the line becomes a staircase on the grid. Each step gets the keys the line reaches in it; a flat part gets one note per step.
Steps count from the line's start. Ticking it takes the Snap box's length; change it here after, in ticks or as a note length like 1/32 or 3/16.
app.too_many_points: Too many points to list ({n}): drag them on the piano roll.
app.ppq_must_be_a_whole_number: PPQ must be a whole number from 1 to 65535
app.bpm_must_be_a_number_at: BPM must be a number, at least 4
