panel_custom.one_long_note_per_key_insid: One long note per key inside.
panel_custom.the_inside_filled_with_back: The inside filled with back-to-back notes of one gate.
panel_custom.just_the_outline_chopped_in: Just the outline, chopped into notes of one gate.
panel_custom.nested_tip: The inside filled with smaller and smaller copies of the shape, one inside the other. Each step gets a colour of its own (with Multi channel).
panel_custom.nested_notes_tip: Fill: one long note per key in each step. Spam: chopped into notes of the spam gate.
panel_custom.nested_way_tip: Scaling: each copy is a true smaller copy, shrinking toward the centre point (drag its handle on the piano roll). Even band: every step is equally thick all the way round and follows each bend, like the Outline gate (no centre point). Blend: the steps follow the outline near the edge and round off smoothly into the centre point.
panel_custom.nested_of_tip: What the smaller copies are: the shape itself, or another shape from your library, made to fit the same box. The shape itself stays the outermost step.
panel_custom.nested_morph_tip: The steps change from this shape into the picked one bit by bit: the first step is this shape, the last step is the picked one. Each piece goes with the nearest piece of the other; pieces left over shrink away or grow out of nothing.
panel_custom.nested_angle_tip: Turns the copies by this much, round the centre point, before anything else. Turn adds its turn on top.
panel_custom.nested_mix_tip: 0 % = the same as Even band. 100 % = the steps round off fully into the centre point. Values in between mix the two.
panel_custom.nested_steps_tip: How many copies. The shape itself counts as the first one.
panel_custom.nested_last_tip: How big the last, smallest copy is. 0 % = the copies shrink down to a point.
panel_custom.nested_spacing_tip: 0 = even steps. Above 0: the steps get closer together toward the last copy. Below 0: closer together near the outline.
panel_custom.nested_turn_tip: Each copy is turned a little more than the one before it (measured as the shape was first drawn).
panel_custom.nested_colours_tip: How many channels the steps take turns over. Each one is a colour of its own with Multi channel.
panel_custom.nested_skip_tip: Leaves every other step without notes, so the copies show as separate rings.
panel_custom.tiles_tip: The inside filled with another shape repeated like wallpaper, cut where it meets the outline. Each tile gets a colour of its own by where it is (with Multi channel). Drag the small handle to slide the tiles.
panel_custom.tiles_of_tip: The shape every tile is made of, from your library. It fills the tile's box.
panel_custom.tiles_keys_tip: How many keys tall one tile is.
panel_custom.tiles_length_tip: How long one tile is, in ticks.
panel_custom.tiles_gap_keys_tip: Empty keys between one row of tiles and the next.
panel_custom.tiles_gap_tip: Empty ticks between two tiles side by side.
panel_custom.tiles_layout_tip: Grid: the tiles in straight rows and columns. Bricks: every other row moved half a tile sideways, like a brick wall.
panel_custom.tiles_flip_tip: Flips every other tile, so neighbours mirror each other. Both: every other row upside down and every other column side to side.
panel_custom.tiles_by_tip: Which colour each tile gets, by where it is: the next colour along each diagonal, column or row, a checkerboard (2 colours), or one colour for all.
panel_custom.tiles_colours_tip: How many channels the tiles take turns over. Each one is a colour of its own with Multi channel.
panel_custom.tiles_whole_tip: Leaves out every tile the outline cuts, so only whole tiles are left.
panel_custom.tiles_too_many: Too many tiles for this shape, so it's left empty. Make the tiles bigger or the gaps wider.
panel_custom.tiles_needs_multi: Tiles get their colours only with Channels set to Multi channel.
panel_custom.nested_needs_multi: Nested steps get their colours only with Channels set to Multi channel.
panel_custom.ripples_tip: Rings that grow out from the shapes drawn inside the outline, each one a bigger copy of its shape. Where the rings of two shapes meet, the smaller one wins. The outer outline only cuts the rings off; with no outer outline they grow out freely. Each ring gets a colour of its own (with Multi channel).
panel_custom.ripples_steps_tip: How many rings, counting the ones inside the drawn shapes.
panel_custom.ripples_grow_tip: How big the biggest ring is, compared with the shape as drawn. Greyed while Auto is ticked.
panel_custom.ripples_trim_tip: The rings stop at the outer outline. Off: they grow past it, as far as Grow to says (Auto can't be used then). Cut them by hand with the Slice tool.
panel_custom.ripples_auto_tip: The biggest ring grows just far enough to fill the whole outline. Only with an outer outline and Cut at the outline ticked.
panel_custom.ripples_turn_tip: Each ring is turned a little more than the one inside it. The ring on each drawn shape stays as drawn, and the rings inside it turn the other way.
panel_custom.ripples_spacing_tip: 0 = even rings. Above 0: the small rings closer together. Below 0: the big rings closer together.
panel_custom.ripples_colours_tip: How many channels the rings take turns over. Each one is a colour of its own with Multi channel. The ring just inside each drawn shape is always the first colour.
panel_custom.ripples_skip_tip: Leaves every other ring without notes, so the rings show as separate bands.
panel_custom.ripples_edge_tip: A ring always ends exactly on each shape you drew, so its outline shows in the pattern. Off: the rings are spread evenly and may run across it.
panel_custom.ripples_inside_tip: What goes inside the drawn shapes. Rings: the rings carry on inside them. Empty: no notes inside them. Plain: one colour inside them.
panel_custom.ripples_none: Draw a closed shape for the ripples to grow from.
panel_custom.ripples_picked_tip: The shape inside whose centre point you clicked on the piano roll. Its rings can turn their own way and grow from their own spot.
panel_custom.ripples_picked_turn_tip: How this shape's rings turn: the same as all (Turn above), the other way round, or by their own amount.
panel_custom.ripples_picked_centre_tip: Where this shape's rings grow from, in the shape's box: u = 0 % at its left side to 100 % at its right, v = 0 % at its bottom to 100 % at its top. Drag its centre point on the piano roll, or right-click it to put it back in the middle.
panel_custom.ripples_needs_multi: Ripples get their colours only with Channels set to Multi channel.
panel_custom.borders_tip: Where two areas of different colours meet (coloured in the drawer's Areas tool), the notes there go to the outline too. Off: the outline is only where the filled part ends.
panel_custom.too_many_colours: This shape needs {n} colours, but a shape can have at most {most} (the outline and the plain fill count too). The extra colours share the last one.
panel_custom.normal_all_its_notes_togeth:
Normal: all its notes together.
Outline: the notes along the edge of what's filled go on a channel of their own
and the inside's on another (the same gate, so they line up). Needs Channels: Multi channel.
panel_custom.channels_isn_t_multi_channe: Channels isn't Multi channel now, so it's all one channel (turns orange).
panel_custom.fill_and_spam_where_outline:
Fill and Spam: where outlines overlap, the overlap is left empty
(a shape inside a shape makes a hole). Off: everything the lines close in is filled,
overlaps and holes too, also where one line crosses itself.
panel_custom.each_key_s_notes_start_at:
Each key's notes start at that key's left edge,
so the left side is exact and the right side ragged.
panel_custom.every_note_sits_on_the_gate:
Every note sits on the gate grid counted from the start of the song,
so the notes form straight columns (lined up with bar lines and
other shapes); both sides are a little ragged.
panel_custom.centred_tip:
What doesn't fit a whole gate is shared between both ends of each key,
so a peak or a point comes out the same on both sides.
panel_custom.range_tip: Opens a window where the gate can go from one number to another across the shape (left to right, low to high or top to bottom), along a graph you can change. Every whole-tick gate in between gets an equal share, like a gate distribution: most notes get the short gates.
panel_custom.gate_ranged_tip: A gate Range is on: the gate goes from {a} to {b} ticks across the shape (Range… changes it). Changing this number takes the Range off, back to one gate for every note.
panel_custom.ends_tip:
What happens to the bit of each key that doesn't fit a whole gate.
Pictures of each: Help (F1) → Inside fill.
panel_custom.edge_tip:
Makes the outline at least this thick, so it doesn't get thin where the shape is steep. 0 = off.
It grows into the inside, so the shape's edge stays where it is. Where the shape is thinner than that, all of it becomes outline.
Works with Empty, Outline spam, and Fill / Spam set to "Outline". Lines that don't close have no inside and stay as they are.
panel_custom.edge_mode_tip:
Even band: the inside shrinks the same way on every side, top and bottom too, measured as the shape looked when it was first drawn (so a circle shrinks into a smaller circle), so the outline is equally thick all round, holes and inner corners included.
Grow sideways: each short outline note just grows longer toward the middle of its key.
colours.shift_tip:
Each key row starts on a different channel: every few keys up, the turns start this many channels later, so one colour makes slanted lines instead of straight stripes.
0 = off. 1 = one way, -1 = the other way; bigger numbers make flatter lines, more keys make steeper ones.
Rows are counted from the shape's lowest key. Works with Each key row too.
colours.rows_tip:
From its start: each key row starts again at the first channel where its notes begin, so the colours follow the shape's left edge instead of making straight stripes.
From its end: each key row's last note gets the first channel, counting back, so the colours follow the shape's right edge (exact with Ends: Stretch or a short gate).
A row with a gap (like a ring's two sides) starts again after the gap too.
Spam and Outline spam shapes only.
colours.rows_only: None of the picked shapes is Spam or Outline spam: Fill, Empty and lines have one note per piece of a key row, so every note would start again (one colour).
colours.tip:
The notes take turns over several channels, so the colour changes with each turn (which colours you see depends on the program showing the MIDI).
By step: each step the next channel (spam: each gate column; lines: each note in time).
By key: each key the next channel (rows).
By time: a note length from the start of the song, like the snap (1/4 = a beat), so it lines up with the bar lines.
Channels: how many take turns. Every: how long one channel lasts.
Needs Channels: Multi channel.
colours.needs: Channels isn't Multi channel now: all its notes are in one channel, so the colour doesn't change.
recolour.amount_tip_clumps: How rough the edges between the colour areas are: 0 % = a clean cut, 100 % = very ragged.
recolour.amount_tip_scatter: How many notes are torn off their colour onto another one: 0 % = none (as before), 100 % = every note.
recolour.tip:
Changes which colour each note has. The notes stay exactly where they are, with the same gates.
Shuffle: the colours the shape already has are handed out again at random (pasted notes: their own colours; drawn shapes: the colours from Colours).
Split: Scattered: works even on one colour. Notes picked at random are torn off onto another colour (a new one when the shape has only one).
Split: Clumps: the shape is cut into colour areas (bands from left to right by default, more in Shares…), each note taking the colour of the area its middle is in.
Two notes on the same key that sound together keep different colours, so they never cut each other.
With "Repeated colours get new channels", each note stays on the channels of the repeat it was in before the shuffle.
Needs Channels: Multi channel.
recolour.needs: Channels isn't Multi channel now: all its notes are in one channel, so the colours don't change.
recolour.one: This shape has only one colour, so there's nothing to shuffle. Give it more with Colours above, or add new ones in Shares….
recolour.by_tip:
Per note: each note gets its own colour.
Per chord: notes starting at the same time change together and get one colour.
Per run: notes on one key that touch (each starts where the one before ends) change together and get one colour.
recolour.shares_tip: How many colours to use and how much of each.
recolour.mix_tip:
These notes have more than {most} colours, so they're split into colour sets of {most} (in track order).
Off: each note only takes colours from its own set.
On: notes may take a colour from any set.
shares.title: Shares
shares.nothing: Select a shape with Recolour on.
shares.colours_tip:
How many colours each colour set uses: its own colours first, then new ones (new channels).
From {least} (the colours it has) up to {most}.
shares.share_tip:
How likely this colour is for a note that changes colour.
Type a % (25) or a fraction (1/4). All shares always add up to 100 %: the others keep their sizes to each other.
Locked colours never change when you change another one (as far as the locked ones leave room).
Middle-click the knob: back to an even share.
shares.lock_tip:
Lock this colour: its share stays as it is when you change the others or press Even shares.
Click again to unlock it.
shares.mixed_tip: The selected shapes have different shares here. A change gives this share to all of them.
shares.even_tip: Every share the same (locked colours stay as they are).
shares.hint: Notes are picked at random, so the result is close to these shares, not exact.
shares.hint_clumps: Split: Clumps: each share is how big that colour's area is.
shares.area_tip:
How big this colour's area is (the areas go in this order).
Type a % (25) or a fraction (1/4). All shares always add up to 100 %: the others keep their sizes to each other.
Locked colours never change when you change another one (as far as the locked ones leave room).
Middle-click the knob: back to an even share.
shares.pattern_tip:
How the colour areas are laid out.
Bands: stripes across the shape (upright, in time order, until you turn them with Angle).
Swirl: arms that twist around the Centre point.
Wedges: slices around the Centre point.
shares.angle_tip:
Turns the colour areas (-360 to 360 degrees, counter-clockwise).
Drag the knob up / down (Shift: fine), or right-click it to point it. Middle-click: 0.
shares.tight_tip:
How many times the swirl turns from the Centre point to the edge (0 = wedges). It twists most near the centre.
Middle-click: back to 1.
shares.centre_tip:
The point Swirl and Wedges turn around, in % of the shape's box (50 / 50 = the middle).
You can also drag the dot on the shape in the piano roll while this window is open.
shares.push_tip: Bunches the colour areas toward this side, a step a click (the notes never move).
shares.framed: Flipped or turned since: the areas moved with the shape, but these numbers stay as you set them.
recolour.again_tip: A new random result. The same shape always shows the same result until you press this.
recolour.amount_tip: How many notes get a new colour: 0 % = none (as before), 100 % = every note picks one at random.
stir.button_tip:
Turn or twist the colours these notes have now, around a centre point. No colour is added or taken away and nothing is random: only the colours already there move around.
Works with Recolour Off too, and on top of Shuffle and Split.
stir.title: Stir colours
stir.nothing: Select a shape to stir its colours.
liquify.button_tip:
Push the colours around with a brush, like an image editor's Liquify. The notes stay where they are: only which colour each one has changes.
The bends stay with the shape: change its colours later and they follow the same bends.
liquify.title: Liquify
liquify.nothing: Select a shape to liquify its colours.
liquify.hint: Drag over the selected shape on the piano roll to push its colours. Hold Alt for the opposite: Twirl turns the other way, Pinch swells out (Bulge), Freeze takes the mask away (Thaw). Straight strokes: Shift+click the start, then Shift+click the end. Keep holding the second click to push it further. Add Ctrl to snap it to every 15°. Esc forgets the start.
liquify.push_tip: Pushes the colours along the way you drag, like a finger through wet paint.
liquify.restore_tip: Brushes the bends away again, slowly, so the colours go back to how they were.
liquify.smooth_tip: Evens out the bends under the brush: sharp kinks and jagged edges become smoother curves.
liquify.twirl_tip: Swirls the colours around the brush's middle. Hold the mouse still to keep turning. Hold Alt to turn the other way.
liquify.pinch_tip: Draws the colours in toward the brush's middle, so they look smaller there. Hold Alt to Bulge: the colours swell out instead.
liquify.freeze_tip: Paints a red mask over spots the other brushes must leave alone. Hold Alt to Thaw: the mask is taken away, so the brushes work there again.
liquify.twirl_way_tip: Which way Twirl turns the colours. Holding Alt while you brush turns them the other way.
liquify.rate_tip: How fast a held brush keeps working: Restore, Smooth, Twirl, Pinch and Freeze while you hold the mouse still, and every tool while you hold a straight stroke's second click. 0 = only while it moves.
liquify.edge_tip: Where colours come from when a bend reaches past the shape's edge, like the Stir's choice of the same name.
liquify.restore_all_tip: Takes every bend of the selected shapes away. The freeze mask stays.
liquify.show_mask_tip: Shows the frozen spots as a see-through red tint on the piano roll.
liquify.freeze_all_tip: Freezes the whole shape. Then Thaw the spots you want to change.
liquify.thaw_all_tip: Takes the whole freeze mask away.
liquify.invert_all_tip: Swaps the frozen and the free spots.
liquify.size_tip: How wide the brush is on the screen, in pixels. Zooming doesn't change it.
liquify.density_tip: How hard the brush's edge is. High: it pushes as much almost out to its edge. Low: it fades out softly from the middle.
liquify.pressure_tip: How strongly each stroke pushes. Low pressure makes it easier to stop at just the right spot.
liquify.smoothing_tip: Evens out a shaky hand: the brush trails behind the mouse on a string and only moves when the string is pulled tight. Higher = a longer string, smoother strokes.
liquify.needs: Channels isn't Multi channel now: all the notes are in one channel, so liquifying changes nothing.
liquify.one: This shape has only one colour, so there's nothing to push around. Give it more with Colours in the side panel.
liquify.zero: Strength is 0 %, so the bends you brush don't show yet.
liquify.shown_tip: Untick to hide the Liquify bends without losing them; tick to show them again. Brushing shows them again too.
liquify.strength_tip: How far the bends push the colours. 100 % = as brushed, 200 % = twice as far along the same bends, 0 % = none. Up to 400 %.
stir.turn_tip:
Turns all the colours around the Centre point by this much. It can go past a whole turn (360°): the ring changes colour for each further turn. On the whole shape a whole turn looks like none, but inside an Area each extra turn winds the colours tighter towards the area's edge.
Middle-click: back to 0.
stir.twist_tip:
Twists the colours into a swirl around the Centre point: how many times they wind round from the centre to the edge (minus = the other way). It twists most near the centre.
Middle-click: back to 0.
stir.bulge_tip:
Swells the colours out from the middle like a lens (plus), or pinches them in (minus). +100 % makes the middle twice as big, +200 % three times; the colours get packed tighter towards the edge. No colour is added or lost. The knob goes to ±200 %; type up to ±1000 % in the box (on thin stripes very big numbers pack the edge into confetti).
Without an Area it bulges the whole shape round the Centre point; with one it stays inside the area, round the area's middle.
Middle-click: back to 0.
stir.centre_tip:
Where the colours turn and twist around, in % of the shape's box (50 / 50 = the middle). It may go past the box, from -1000 to 1100 %: far away, the colours bend in gentle curves.
With "Moving the Centre point squeezes the colours" ticked, moving it also moves the middle of the colours there: they get squeezed on one side and stretched on the other.
You can also drag the dot on the shape in the piano roll while this window is open. Right-click the dot: back to the middle.
stir.squeeze: Moving the Centre point squeezes the colours
stir.squeeze_tip:
Ticked: moving the Centre point also moves the middle of the colours there, so they get squeezed on one side and stretched on the other.
Unticked: the Centre point only says where the colours turn and twist around. With no Turn or Twist, nothing changes.
stir.add_tip:
Add another stir after these. Each stir bends the colours the stirs before it left, with its own Centre point and settings, so you can put a swirl in one spot and another somewhere else (up to {most} stirs).
The new stir is kept once you change one of its settings.
stir.drop_tip: Take this stir away. The stirs after it then bend the colours the ones before it left.
stir.area_tip:
Whole shape: the stir works on all the colours.
Circle, Square or Diamond: it stirs only the colours inside that area around the Centre point; outside it nothing changes. The stir fades out smoothly towards the area's edge, so there is no seam.
Below the line: the drawings in your shape library. The area takes that drawing's outline (a copy: changing the library later doesn't change it).
stir.draw_hint: Draw the area on the piano roll with any drawing tools: every stroke you draw now goes into the area, nothing that was there before. Open ends are closed with a straight line, as Fill does. Then press "Use as the area".
stir.pick_hint: Click a shape on the piano roll: its outline becomes the area, where it is. The shape itself stays as it is.
stir.pick_status: Click the shape whose outline the Stir area should take.
stir.pick_none: That shape has no inside to stir (only open lines, or no outline), so pick another one.
stir.to_shape_tip: Puts the area on the piano roll as a drawn shape of its own, where the area is. The stirred shape keeps its area.
stir.draw_no_paste: While a Stir area is being drawn, pasting is off: only the strokes you draw go into the area.
stir.draw_no_notes: None of the stirred shapes has notes here, so the area wasn't used (the strokes stay).
stir.hard_tip:
Ticked: the area is cut clean at its edge, like a turntable: inside, Turn and Twist work in full right up to the outline, outside nothing moves.
Unticked: they fade out smoothly towards the edge, so there is no seam.
stir.reverse: Reverse the track order inside the area
stir.reverse_tip: Inside the area, the order of the colours (tracks) is turned round: the first colour becomes the last, the second the one before last, and so on. Each colour set on its own. Outside the area nothing changes.
stir.affects_tip: What only happens inside the area. Untick one to let it work on the whole shape again, while the others stay inside the area.
stir.polar_tip:
Wraps the colours round the Centre point: going round becomes going across, and going out from the middle becomes going up. Straight upright stripes become rays; with Turn at 90° they become rings. In between, the colours are part way there.
Inside an Area (its tick under "The area limits"): round the area's middle, the rings take the area's shape (a Square area gives square rings).
stir.ripple_tip: Moves the colours along a wave, so straight stripes go wavy. Height = how far they move, in % of the shape's box.
stir.ripple_len_tip: How long one wave is, in % of the shape's box.
stir.ripple_kind_tip:
Sideways: the colours move sideways, the wave runs up the shape.
Up and down: the colours move up and down, the wave runs across.
Rings: the colours move out from the Centre point and back, like rings from a water drop.
stir.kaleido_tip: One slice of the colours mirrored round the Centre point, like a kaleidoscope. Slices = how many times it repeats (0 = off, at least 2).
stir.kaleido_turn_tip: Which slice of the colours is mirrored: turns the slice round the Centre point.
stir.wring_tip: Twists the colours like a wrung ribbon along a line through the Centre point: the farther along the line, the more they turn. Turns = how much at the far end (minus = the other way).
stir.wring_angle_tip: The line's angle: 0 = across, 90 = straight up.
stir.round_edge: Round bends at the Area's edge:
stir.round_edge_tip:
How Straight to round and Kaleidoscope end at the Area's edge.
Cut clean: they stop sharply at the edge (a soft fade smears them into stripes).
Fade like the rest: they follow the Hard edge tick, like Turn and Twist.
stir.flip_in_tip: Where the colour flips work: on the whole shape, only inside the area, or only outside it. Needs an Area.
stir.spot_tip: Where the area's middle is when it doesn't move with the Centre point, in % of the shape's box (it may go past the box, from -1000 to 1100 %). Same as dragging the square on the piano roll.
stir.draw_save: Also save it to the shape library
stir.draw_save_tip: Keeps a copy of the drawing in your shape library (it asks for a name), so you can pick it as an area again later.
stir.draw_use_tip: Turns the strokes drawn since you picked "Draw one…" into the area, exactly where you drew them, and takes the strokes away.
stir.draw_cancel_tip: Stops drawing. The strokes stay on the piano roll (Ctrl+Z takes them back) and the area stays as it was.
stir.draw_status: Draw the Stir area on the piano roll, then press "Use as the area" in the Stir window.
stir.draw_none: Draw a shape first: it needs an inside (a single straight line has none).
stir.draw_lost: The stirred shapes changed while drawing: select them and try again.
stir.area_no_inside: "{name}" has no inside to stir (only open lines), so the area wasn't changed.
stir.reach_tip:
The area's base size, in % of the shape's box (for a diamond: from tip to tip), up to 200 % of the box. Stretch makes it wider or taller from there. On a long or tall box the area stretches with it, like Turn does. Counted "of the circle inside", the number can go past 200 on a long shape.
While this window is open the piano roll shows the area as a dashed line: drag the line to change the size.
Tip: untick "Moving the Centre point squeezes the colours" so the area leaves the colours where they are.
stir.angle_tip: How far the area is turned, in degrees. On the piano roll the area has its own box (a solid green line with round handles, unlike a shape's box): drag a side's middle to stretch the area that way, a corner to stretch it both ways (Ctrl on a corner changes Size and keeps its proportions), just outside a corner to turn it (15° steps, Shift for any angle), just outside a side's middle to slant it.
stir.slant_tip: How far the area's top slides sideways, in % of its height (minus = to the left); 0 = not slanted. On the piano roll, drag just outside a side's middle of the area's box to slant it by hand. Slanting the left or right side up or down shows here as Angle and Slant together.
stir.tied: Area moves with the Centre point
stir.tied_tip:
Ticked: the area sits on the Centre point and moves with it.
Unticked: the area stays where it is and gets its own spot, a square on the piano roll: drag the square to move the area (right-click it: back to the middle). Turn and Twist still go round the Centre point, so a Centre point outside the area turns what you see through it around a far point.
stir.round_tip:
Ticked: the area keeps the shape it has on the screen right now, so a circle stays a circle on a long or tall shape, and Size is in % of the box's longer side. Zooming later doesn't change it: press "Match the screen" to take the screen's look again.
Unticked: the area stretches with the shape's box.
stir.stretch_tip: Stretches the area from its Size: "across" makes it wider (over 100 %) or narrower (under 100 %), "up" makes it taller or flatter, from 10 % to 1000 % each. For an oval or a long rectangle on purpose, without turning the area. Works with or without "Round as seen".
stir.spin: Turn and twist round as seen
stir.spin_tip:
Ticked: Turn and Twist turn the colours round the way they look on the screen right now, so a turned stripe keeps its width on a long or tall shape. Zooming later doesn't change it: press "Match the screen" to take the screen's look again.
Unticked: they turn in the shape's own box, so on a long shape a turn squashes and stretches the pattern.
stir.match_tip: "Round as seen" and "Turn and twist round as seen" both take the piano roll's look right now (how tall a key is next to how wide a beat is). Zoom first so the shape looks the way you want, then press this.
stir.hint: Bends the colours the notes have now. Each note takes the colour of the note found where the stir brings it from.
stir.needs: Channels isn't Multi channel now: all the notes are in one channel, so stirring changes nothing.
stir.one: This shape has only one colour, so there's nothing to stir. Give it more with Colours in the side panel.
stir.reset_tip: This stir back to nothing: no turn, no twist, every setting as it starts. With only one stir, the colours go back to how they were before.
stir.middle_tip: Puts this stir's Centre point back in the middle of the shape (50 / 50).
stir.flip_tip:
Mirrors the colours, before this stir bends them or its finished pattern (see Flip what). The notes stay where they are.
Sideways: each key row's colours from end to start. Upside down: the colours from top to bottom.
The colours flip at the shape's own outline, so a round or slanted shape flips into itself.
stir.edge_tip:
What happens to colours stirred past the edge of the shape.
Escape: they're gone, and the colours at the edge stretch in to fill the gaps.
Wrap around: what goes out one side comes back in on the other side of the notes, as if the colours were a repeating tile.
Cut by the outline: the stir is worked out on the box around the shape, and the outline cuts it out. On a round or slanted shape, spots that come from the empty parts of the box take the nearest note's colour.
Bend with the outline: each key row is stretched to fill the box first, so the stir follows the shape's outline and never comes from empty space.
stir.fold_tip:
Click to fold or unfold this part.
Folded, the grey words say what it's set to.
stir.short_spin: turn and twist round as seen
stir.flip_by_tip:
How the sideways flip swaps the colours in each key row.
Time: mirrored across the row from its first note's start to its last note's end; each note takes the colour of the note at its mirrored time.
Note order: the row's 1st note swaps colours with its last, the 2nd with the one before last, and so on, whatever their lengths. A row with one note keeps its colour.
stir.flip_of_tip:
What the colour flips mirror.
The colours, then stir: the colours are flipped first, then this stir bends them, so a swirl stays at the Centre point.
The stirred pattern: this stir's finished pattern is mirrored, like the normal flips but only the colours: a swirl turns over with it, and with "only that part" it turns over inside the area. The notes stay where they are.
stir.mirror_tip:
With the flips only inside (or outside) the area: what they mirror across.
The whole shape: each key row's whole width and the shape's whole height, so an area off to one side shows colours from the shape's other side.
Only that part: only the notes being flipped count, so the part inside the area flips in place.
stir.smooth_tip:
The flips mirror each key row across its own notes, so the colours flip into the shape and never into empty space. Where the outline has a corner (a triangle's tip, an area cut off by the shape's edge), that mirror line turns sharply and leaves a straight seam in the colours.
Smooth corners rounds the line through those corners, over this much of the shape's height (its width for Upside down). 0 = sharp, as before. Straight outlines don't change.
stir.bend_smooth_tip:
Bend with the outline stretches each key row to the shape's whole width. Where the outline has a corner, the rows' widths change sharply and leave a straight seam in the colours.
Smooth corners rounds those corners, over this much of the shape's height. 0 = sharp, as before. Only for Bend with the outline.
stir.size_of_tip:
What 100 % Size is.
Of the box: the shape's box (its longer side with "Round as seen").
Of the circle inside: the biggest circle that fits inside the box, so 100 % touches its shorter sides; Size can go past 200 % then, up to as big as the box's own 200 %. Without "Round as seen" the area stretches with the box, and this is the same as the box.
Of the circle around: the smallest circle round the whole box, so a round area at 100 % reaches its corners too.
Switching keeps the area as big as it is: only the Size number changes.
stir.sets_tip:
This shape has more than one set of channels (15 colours each, 16 with channel 10).
Stay in their set: each note keeps its own set of tracks and takes the matching colour in it, so the pattern bends as a whole.
Move between sets: each note takes the colour and track of the note it's stirred from, so notes can end up in another set.
panel_custom.hz_not_merged: Not on a merged shape (Gate sensitive merge): split it first.
panel_custom.hz_tip:
Spam so fast that the repeats sound like a tone.
The gate is worked out from the tone, the BPM and the PPQ, and gates of two sizes
(like 34 and 35 ticks) are mixed so the tone comes out exact. Every key is in step.
Best heard after the MIDI is rendered to an audio file.
panel_custom.hz_skipped: Some of the selected shapes are Hz bass. A Hz bass gets its gate from its tone, so it stays as it is: only the other shapes change.
panel_custom.hz_range_off: A gate Range doesn't work together with Hz bass, so it's switched off. Unticking Hz bass brings it back, with the gate it had.
panel_custom.hz_cents_tip: Pitch adjustment: 100 cents = one key up, -100 = one key down.
panel_custom.hz_short: The gates are short, so the tone wobbles: a higher PPQ fixes it.
panel_custom.hz_stale: The tempo under this Hz bass changed since it was made (or it was moved to another tempo), so its tone is off now.
panel_custom.hz_gates_tip:
Auto: Fixed for a note that holds still when it's off by no more than the threshold,
else Alternating. A slide is always Alternating.
Alternating: gates of two sizes take turns, so the tone is exact.
Fixed: every gate is the same whole number of ticks, so the tone is a little off
(the higher the PPQ, the less).
panel_custom.hz_notes_tip:
Opens the Hz bass window: place notes there and the tone follows them.
Notes at the same time make a chord; the red line is the tone you really hear.
panel_custom.hz_short_fixed: The gates are short, so the tone is off: a higher PPQ fixes it.
panel_custom.hz_tool_info: Drag up or down on the piano roll where the Hz bass should start: that is the keys it repeats. Then place its notes in the window that opens.
panel_polygon.points_tip: How many corners (3 = triangle, 4 = square, 5 = pentagon…), or how many points a star has.
panel_polygon.kind_tip:
Polygon: straight sides, a flat side at the bottom.
Star: outer and inner points take turns.
Crossing star: every Skip-th point joined by straight lines that cross (5 points, skip 2 = a pentagram).
panel_polygon.inner_tip: Star: how far out the inner points are, in % of the outer ones (smaller = thinner points, 100 = a polygon with twice the points).
panel_polygon.skip_tip: Crossing star: each point is joined to the one this many points further round (1 = a plain polygon). When it shares a divisor with Points it makes several loops (6 points, skip 2 = two triangles).
panel_custom.they_keep_their_own_velocit: They keep their own velocities until you change the velocity here. The velocity pane changes only the notes you draw over.
panel_custom.drag_a_corner_or_side_to: Drag a corner or side to stretch them, just outside a corner to turn them, just outside a side's middle to skew them.
panel_custom.the_outline_has_a_gap_it: The outline has a gap: it's filled as if a straight line closed it (the dashed line).
panel_custom.the_outline_has_gaps_each_i: The outline has {gaps} gaps: each is closed with a straight line (the dashed lines).
panel_custom.ends_that_nearly_touch_1_64:
Ends that nearly touch (1/64 beat, 1 key) are joined; open parts that are almost
straight aren't filled. Close the gaps yourself to decide where the edge goes.
panel_custom.live_shape_what_you_draw_go: Live shape: what you draw goes into one custom shape (a new one now). Close its outline (points snap onto its ends) to fill it.
panel_custom.drag_a_box_on_the_piano: Drag a box on the piano roll, or click two corners (Ctrl = a perfect {tool} on screen).
panel_custom.pick_a_shape_or_make_one: Pick a shape, or make one with Drawer…
panel_custom.one_gap_in_the_outline_fill: One gap in the outline: filled as if the dashed line closed it.
panel_custom.areas_need_fill: Its areas coloured in the drawer count only with Fill or Spam.
panel_custom.areas_need_multi: Its areas coloured in the drawer get channels of their own only with Multi channel (Project).
panel_custom.gaps_in_the_outline_filled_: {gaps} gaps in the outline: filled as if the dashed lines closed them.
panel_custom.drag_a_box_on_the_piano_2: Drag a box on the piano roll, or click two corners, to place it (Ctrl = keep its proportions).
panel_custom.drag_a_corner_or_side_to_2: Drag a corner or side to resize, just outside a corner to turn it, just outside a side's middle to skew it.
panel_custom.live_shape_what_you_draw_no: Live shape: what you draw now goes into this shape.
panel_custom.picked_stroke_of_del_delete: Picked: stroke {stroke} of {n} (Del = delete it, Ctrl+C / H / J / arrows = copy, flip, turn it, Esc = unpick). Select tool: click a stroke of the selected shape to pick it.
panel_custom.save_the_drawing_to_the_sha: Save the drawing to the shape library as:
panel_custom.is_already_in_the_library_r:
"{name}" is already in the library. Replace it?
Shapes already placed on the piano roll stay as they are.
panel_text.font_size_the_number_is_the:
Font size: the number is the font size in keys, like a font size anywhere
(capital letters come out smaller than that).
Rows: capital letters are exactly that many keys tall.
The number stays the same when you switch, so the text changes size.
panel_text.extra_room_between_letters_in:
Extra room between letters, in 1/1000 of the font size (tracking).
Minus numbers pull the letters closer together.
panel_text.room_between_lines_in_of_the:
Room between lines, in % of the font's own line spacing.
Player down: room between the columns.
panel_text.how_much_of_a_key_s:
How much of a key's height has to be inside a letter for that key to play there
(Fill / Spam only). 50% = the key's middle. Lower = chunkier letters, higher = thinner.
panel_text.makes_the_letters_strokes_thi:
Makes the letters' strokes thicker, in keys (minus = thinner),
as the text looked on screen when it was typed. Big values can look odd in tight corners.
panel_text.pick_the_font_you_can_type: Pick the font (you can type its name in the window that opens).
panel_text.direction_tip:
Which way the letters go.
Piano roll: along time, reads normally here.
Player across: reads across the keys in a falling-notes player; each new line arrives before the one above it.
Player down: the letters arrive one after another in steady steps, first letter first;
each new line is a column beside it (higher keys), arriving at the same time.
The player choices set Letter turn to 90 and tick Flip letters, so the letters stand upright in a player.
panel_text.letter_turn_tip:
Turns each letter on its own spot (anticlockwise, as the piano roll shows it).
90 with Flip letters ticked = upright in a falling-notes player.
panel_text.flip_letters_tip: Turns each letter upside down before Letter turn turns it.
panel_text.isn_t_installed_on_this_pc: "{font}" isn't installed on this PC. The letters stay as they were saved; editing the text redraws all of it in {default}.
panel_text.font_missing_edit:
{fonts} isn't installed on this PC. Editing redraws the whole text in {default}.

Go on?
panel_text.typing_enter_new_line_esc_don: Typing: Enter = new line, Esc = done. Click somewhere else for a new text, on a text to retype it.
panel_text.click_on_the_piano_roll_and: Click on the piano roll and type. Click a text to retype it.
panel_text.double_click_the_text_or_righ: Double-click the text (or right-click → Edit text) to retype it.
panel_text.changes_go_to_all_selected_te: Changes go to all {n} selected texts.
panel_funnel.back_to_back_notes_lined_up: Back-to-back notes, lined up in columns on every key.
panel_funnel.one_note_per_key_from_where: One note per key, from where it joins the funnel to the wall.
panel_funnel.the_notes_stop_at_the_wall: The notes stop at the wall.
panel_funnel.one_more_column_of_notes_on:
One more column of notes on the other side of the wall,
as long as the wall gate.
panel_funnel.spam_gate_with_long_notes_t: Spam gate (with long notes: the column past the wall). Enter to apply.
panel_funnel.gate_ranged_tip: A gate Range is on: the gate goes from {a} ticks at the line start to {b} ticks at the wall (Range… changes it). Changing this number takes the Range off, back to one gate for every note.
panel_funnel.hz_tip: Hz bass: the whole funnel becomes one Hz bass, both sides of the wall. Every key repeats so fast it sounds like a tone, wherever it would play a long note. Notes… opens the window to place notes, chords and slides; they count from the funnel's first beat, and the funnel keeps its length.
panel_funnel.range_tip: Opens a window where the gate can go from one number at the line start to another at the wall, along a graph you can change: smoothly or in steps that halve or double, evenly or as the funnel opens.
panel_funnel.now_draw_the_wall_ctrl_cent: Now draw the wall (Ctrl = centred on the line, right-click = cancel).
panel_funnel.highlighted_right_click_cur: Highlighted: {parts}. Right-click = curve shapes, Del = delete, Esc = clear. Ctrl+click = one more / one less.
panel_funnel.middle_click_on_the_line_to: Middle-click on the line to start a curve there.  A line drawn to its wall = one more line.
panel_funnel.middle_click_the_line_new_c: Middle-click the line = new curve, near a curve = anchor. Select tool: click a curve again = highlight.
panel_funnel.draw_the_funnel_s_line_then: Draw the funnel's line, then its wall (drag, or click twice each).
help.search_type_words_all_of_them: Search: type words (all of them have to be in the topic)
help.show_a_tip_the_first_time: Show a tip the first time I use something
help.nothing_found_try_fewer_or_other: Nothing found. Try fewer or other words.
help.done_every_tip_shows_again_the: Done: every tip shows again the next time.
updates.question_text: Spiderweb can look on GitHub for a newer version when it starts, and tell you when there is one (with what's new in it). It only asks GitHub for the list of versions: nothing about you or your work is sent, and nothing is downloaded by itself.
updates.question_later: You can change this any time in Settings (Help → Settings… in the menu bar).
backup.title: Settings backed up
backup.head: Older settings found
updates.restarting: Downloaded and checked. Spiderweb closes and starts the new version…
updates.zip_ready:
Downloaded and checked: {file}

Unzip it over your Spiderweb folder to update. Your own files in the user folder stay as they are.
updates.fail.no_check: Spiderweb can't check downloads here, so please use the download page.
updates.fail.unsigned: This version has no safety signature, so it can't be updated from here. Please use the download page.
updates.fail.not_writable: Spiderweb can't save files in its folder, so it can't update itself. Please use the download page.
updates.fail.bad_signature: The download didn't pass the safety check, so it wasn't used. Someone may have changed the files on GitHub: please don't install this version, and report it.
updates.fail.bad_file: The downloaded file doesn't match its safety signature, so it was deleted. Please don't install this version, and report it.
updates.fail.wrong_version: The download's safety signature is for another version, so it wasn't used. Please don't install this version, and report it.
updates.fail.too_big: The download was much bigger than it should be, so it was stopped.
updates.fail.no_connection: The download stopped. Check your internet connection and try again.
updates.fail.swap_failed: Spiderweb couldn't replace its own file (another program may be using it). Nothing was changed.
updates.fail.not_closed: Spiderweb wasn't closed, so the update was put back. Press the button again to update.
updates.fail.other: Something went wrong while updating. Nothing was changed.
updates.fail.busy: Another download is still running. Please wait for it to finish.
updates.fail.disk: Spiderweb couldn't save the download (the disk may be full, or another program is using the file). Nothing was changed.

settings.stack_tip:
Which note shows where notes lie on top of each other on one key.
Later track on top: the note of the track lower in the track list, like many MIDI programs.
Louder note on top: the loudest one (equally loud: the later track's). Handy in dense MIDIs, where quiet notes covering the keys hide the music.
Later shape on top: the note of the shape made later (a loaded MIDI's notes: the later track's).
Selected shapes always show on top. A loaded MIDI's note is a little darker where a hidden note under it starts or ends.
settings.hidden_shade_hint:
Your own notes get a little darker where a note hidden under them starts or ends, so you can see notes that are covered.
A loaded MIDI's notes always show this.
settings.keep_offrange_tip:
Shapes keep the notes they make below the lowest key, above the highest key and before the first beat. They're drawn see-through.
They're kept only in the project file: they're never exported, played or copied to other programs, unless Wrap them around is ticked.
settings.wrap_offrange: Wrap them around in exports and Domino copies
settings.wrap_offrange_tip:
The kept notes past the keys are exported, played and copied put back onto the keys: one key above the highest key lands on the lowest key, one key below the lowest lands on the highest (by the project's Keys: 128 or 256).
Notes before bar 1 are always left out.
Off: the kept notes are left out.
settings.keep_offrange_off: Turn on Space past the keys or Space before the start first.
settings.show_wrapped_tip:
Where the kept notes land once they're wrapped around, drawn faintly under your notes, so you see what will be exported and played.
Selected shapes: only for the shapes you selected, with a dashed box round where they land. Always: for every shape.
Red = a wrapped note lands on a note that's already there.
settings.keep_opacity_tip: How strongly the notes kept past the keys and before the start are drawn: 100 % = like other notes, lower = more see-through.
settings.space_keys_tip:
Lets you scroll and move shapes below the lowest key and above the highest key. No notes are made there, unless Keep notes made there is ticked.
The number is how far: 1 = one keyboard's height up and down.
settings.space_bars_tip: Lets you scroll and move shapes before the first beat. No notes are made there, unless Keep notes made there is ticked.
settings.keep_colours_hint:
Multi channel: a shape (plain notes too) that overlaps an earlier one moves whole to the next row of channels (15 further, 16 with channel 10 used), so its colours stay the same. Off: it takes the next free channels (other colours).
Many shapes on top of each other make many tracks: untick Keep empty tracks under Multi channel to write only the tracks with notes.
settings.copy_notes: Ctrl+C also copies as Spiderweb Notes
settings.copy_notes_hint: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+X also put the finished music on the clipboard in a format other MIDI programs can read: notes, tempo, time and key signatures, controllers, track names and colours. Only useful if a program you use reads it. Large copies take a moment longer.
settings.copy_domino_hint: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+X also do what Copy to Domino does, so Ctrl+V in Domino pastes the notes too. Large copies take a moment longer. A copy that would need a question (over a million notes, not enough memory) skips the Domino part: use Copy to Domino for those.
settings.domino_256_hint: Copy, Paste and Export to Domino keep notes above key 127 (256 keys projects). Only the unofficial 256 keys mod of Domino can open them: normal Domino draws them wrong or closes. Keys above 127 sound like keys 0-127 (MIDI sound has 128 keys).
settings.indexes_hint: After a slow Load MIDI, Spiderweb offers to save where everything is in that file, so it opens in a moment next time. A changed MIDI file is read again the usual way.

language.template_tip: Saves a copy of the English texts as the folder lang/_template next to Spiderweb and opens it. Fill in the "language" line at the top of main.json (e.g. 한국어 (Korean)) and the texts, one file at a time if you like (the Help pages are the .txt files in help), then rename the folder (e.g. ko). Texts you leave in English follow Spiderweb's English after an update. Longer words? Add "size.panel_width": 400 to main.json for a wider side panel (also size.tooltip_width, size.tip_width and size.help_width; English: 330, 560, 380, 900).

panel_freehand.makes_the_freehand_stroke:
Makes the freehand stroke perfect: 0 = as you drew it. Higher = straighter lines and smoother curves,
and a stroke that ends where it started becomes a perfect circle, ellipse, square, rectangle or triangle.
The higher, the simpler (a slightly oval loop: an ellipse, then a circle). The stroke as drawn is kept,
so you can change this any time. New freehand strokes use the last number picked.
panel_gliss.grids_tip:
The grid sizes a run's step can be. The step picks itself: the grid nearest
one key per step for the line you drew. Halves = 1/1, 1/2, 1/4 … as fine as the PPQ allows.
Grids shorter than one tick are skipped.
panel_gliss.list_tip:
Your own grid sizes, separated by commas, like 1/16, 1/32, 1/48.
Press Enter to use them.
panel_gliss.step_tip:
How long each step of the run is. Auto = picks itself from how steep
the line is (the grid nearest one key per step). A fixed step keeps the run's
start and keys: 1/32 -> 1/64 makes it 2x faster and half as long.
panel_gliss.copies_tip:
Copies of the run, each one picked key further above or below it,
playing at the same times. 0 = none.
On the piano roll: drag the selected run's dotted lines up or down.
panel_gliss.len_tip:
How long each note is: % of the step (100 % = up to the next note,
150 % = they overlap), or ticks. With "Where the line crosses" or "Smooth":
% of the gap up to the next note. On the piano roll: drag any note's right end.
panel_gliss.timing_tip:
On the grid: one note per step, one after another.
Where the line crosses: each note starts where the line crosses its key,
so a curve speeds up where it's steep and slows down where it's flat.
Smooth: the same keys, start and end as "Where the line crosses",
but the speed changes gradually, so the run sounds even.
panel_gliss.smooth_tip:
How even the run's speed is: 0 % = the notes start where the line crosses,
100 % = every gap the same. In between, the speed still follows the bend
but changes gradually. The notes may sit off the line: it sounds smoother.
panel_gliss.no_picks:
No keys picked: runs use the white keys.
Click the piano keys to pick keys
(Ctrl+click: just that one key).

help.select.words: move pick choose drag box rectangle marquee area double right-click switch toggle last tool
help.line.title: Line (L)
help.line.tip: Drag from start to end, or click the start and then click the end.
help.poly.title: Polyline (P)
help.poly.tip: Click point after point (or drag each piece). Double-click or right-click to finish.
help.free.title: Freehand (F)

help.free.words: draw hand pencil smooth straighten shape recognition
help.curve.title: Curve (C)
help.curve.tip: Drag from start to end (or click both), then bend it with its blue handles. Middle-click the curve to add an anchor.
help.arc.title: Arc (A)
help.arc.tip: Click the start, a point it passes through, and the end. Or drag from start to end, then move the mouse to bend it and click.
help.gliss.title: Glissando (R)
help.gliss.tip: Drag a line: a run of short notes, one on each picked key, one grid step each. Click the piano keys on the left to pick the keys (a click = that note in every octave).

help.funnel.title: Funnel (N)
help.funnel.tip: Draw its line, then its wall (drag, or click twice each). Then middle-click on the line to start a curve there.
help.text.title: Text (X)
help.text.tip: Click on the piano roll and type. Esc = done. The letters become a custom shape.

help.by_snap.title: Notes by snap

help.drawer.title: The drawer
help.drawer.tip: Draw a shape for your library, Save it, then Use on the piano roll. Closed outlines can be filled.
help.drawer_select.title: Drawer: Select and editing
help.drawer_select.tip: Drag a point (small squares) or a stroke. Drag on empty space = a box selecting several. Del = delete.
help.drawer_select.words: drawer edit move copy flip turn
help.drawer_line.title: Drawer: Line
help.drawer_line.tip: Drag from start to end, or click both.
help.drawer_poly.title: Drawer: Polyline
help.drawer_poly.tip: Click points (or drag each piece). Click the first point again to close it.
help.drawer_free.title: Drawer: Freehand
help.drawer_free.tip: Drag to draw. Let go near the start to close it.
help.drawer_curve.title: Drawer: Curve
help.drawer_curve.tip: From start to end, then bend it with its blue handles. Middle-click it = new anchor.
help.drawer_arc.title: Drawer: Arc
help.drawer_arc.tip: Click start, a point it passes through, end. Or drag start to end, then click to bend.
help.drawer_square.title: Drawer: Square
help.drawer_square.tip: Corner to corner. Ctrl = a perfect square.
help.drawer_circle.title: Drawer: Circle
help.drawer_circle.tip: Corner to corner. Ctrl = a perfect circle.
help.drawer_erase.title: Drawer: Eraser
help.drawer_erase.tip: Click a stroke to remove it, or drag a box: every stroke it touches goes. Ctrl+Z = undo.
help.drawer_areas.title: Drawer: Areas
help.drawer_areas.tip: Click an area to give it the colour picked on the right (or Empty), or drag across several. Right-click = back to normal.

help.drawer_slice.title: Drawer: Slice
help.drawer_slice.tip: Drag a line across strokes to cut them there. A circle or square is cut only when the line goes all the way through it.

companion.experimental:
Draw on Domino is experimental. It works from the outside: it follows Domino's window and puts notes in through Domino's own commands and clipboard. It has been tested, but not every song, setting and order of actions can be, so things could still go wrong: notes in the wrong place or missing, a step Ctrl+Z doesn't take back, or Domino closing.

Use it with care: save your song in Domino first and keep a backup of songs that matter.

The safe way is always there: draw in Spiderweb, then Copy to Domino (Ctrl+Shift+C) and paste in Domino.

Start drawing on Domino?
